children: By Alexander Gladstone, Andrew Scurria and Jodi Xu Klein

L'Oréal has engaged restructuring advisers to explore options for mounting U.S. legal liabilities stemming from its use of talc and other chemical ingredients in some of its cosmetic products, according to people familiar with the matter.

L'Oréal's U.S. subsidiary is working with restructuring counsel Weil Gotshal & Manges and investment bank Ducera Partners to address mass lawsuits from individuals alleging that the talc products have caused illness, the people said. L'Oréal also faces allegations that its hair-relaxing products caused users to develop cancer.
The company is considering moving tort liabilities into a separate corporate entity for the purpose of unloading them through a sale to an outside investor, the people said.
Representatives for L'Oréal, Weil and Ducera didn't respond to requests for comment.

Mass talc litigation in recent years has pushed companies to explore restructuring options to resolve claims. Consumer-goods manufacturers, including Avon Products and Johnson & Johnson, have turned to bankruptcy court in recent years to deal with an avalanche of lawsuits alleging that cosmetic talc caused cancer. Talc suppliers such as Whittaker Clark & Daniels, Imerys Talc America and Barrett Minerals have also used chapter 11 to stem mass litigation.
